description: Closed object-class taxonomy for dual-endpoint perception (C12). All ObservationLabel.class_id values MUST be one of these ids — on the robot end (Daedalus) and on the headset end (Eidolon) alike. A class the two ends need but this file lacks is a PR against this file, never a locally invented string: the whole point of the fusion contract is that 'cup' from the headset and 'cup' from the robot are the same term.

classes.definition: Geometry was observed and localised, but the class was NOT determined. This is a real observation with an undetermined class — NOT a placeholder for a class this taxonomy is missing (that is a registry PR) and NOT a way to publish a label the producer does not believe in.
Open-topped drinking vessel, with or without a handle. An open vessel wide enough to eat from is 'bowl'; a closed/necked vessel is 'bottle'.
Necked container, typically capped (water/drink bottle, dispenser bottle). Distinguished from 'cup' by the narrowed neck.
Rigid cylindrical metal container (drink can, tin).
Open round vessel, wider than it is tall.
Flat or shallow dish.
Flat carrier with a raised rim, used to move several objects at once.
Rigid rectangular container, open or closed.
Wide-mouthed container with a screw or clamp lid.
Large open receptacle objects are dropped into (waste bin, parts basket, tote).
Hand-held eating implement — fork, knife, spoon, chopsticks.
Driver tool for screws, any tip type.
Tool that applies torque to a nut or bolt.
Striking tool with a weighted head.
Hinged gripping tool.
Hinged cutting tool with two blades.
Hand-held writing or marking implement.
Bristled implement for cleaning or applying (paint brush, cleaning brush).
Rigid geometric primitive used as a manipulation target (cube, cuboid, cylinder peg).
Rigid or soft sphere.
Flat deformable textile — towel, rag, garment laid out.
Deformable carrier with an opening (plastic bag, pouch, backpack).
Edible item handled as a single object (fruit, vegetable, packaged snack).
Bound book, notebook, or stack of paper handled as one object.
Hand-held mobile phone or similar slab device.
Portable computer with a hinged screen.
Detached computer keyboard.
Computer pointing device.
Hand-held button device — TV remote, game controller, XR controller.
Fixed actuator mounted on a surface — light switch, push button, valve handle.
Graspable fixture attached to a door, drawer, or appliance. The moving panel itself is 'door' or 'drawer'.
Hinged or sliding panel that opens a room, cabinet, or appliance.
Sliding compartment in a cabinet or desk.
Horizontal work surface on legs. The surface objects rest on, not the objects.
Horizontal storage surface mounted above the floor, or the rack holding several.
Seat for one person.
Enclosed storage unit; its openings are 'door' / 'drawer'.
A whole human body in the scene. Safety-relevant: a fused label with class 'person' is what a consumer keys a keep-out volume off.
A human hand observed as an object in the map. Per-joint hand skeletons are NOT this — they travel as canonical frame `observation.hand.*` (C11).
A robot manipulator observed in the scene (typically by the headset end, seeing the robot it teleoperates).
The end-effector of a manipulator, when observed separately from the arm.
A localised volume to avoid whose identity does not matter — use when the class is irrelevant, NOT when it is undetermined (that is 'unknown').
